sports.label: NHL

brain.approach: Score- and opponent-adjusted 5v5 expected-goals ratings, goals-for/against and finishing ratings, rest and back-to-backs → a Poisson regression for each team's regulation goals → an exact score distribution with empirical score effects by period and lead, goalie-pull dynamics, 3-on-3 overtime and the shootout → every market's fair price, decomposed exactly into its factors. Goalie GSAx drives the goalie scenarios; special-teams ratings are measured and shown but left the price on 2026-10-13 (no out-of-sample benefit).
brain.why: Hockey is low-scoring and noisy: goals are a weak signal, shot quality (xG) is a stronger and more stable one (macdonald2012). Leaders sit back and trailing teams pull the goalie, so margins and totals are not plain Poisson (tulsky2012, beaudoin2010). A full distribution, not a single number, is what the moneyline, the puck line and the total all need.

sports.label: MLB

brain.approach: A point-in-time run model: team offence and run prevention, a decayed park factor and a shrunk starting-pitcher effect in a log-linear Poisson fit refreshed every game date, with negative-binomial overdispersion and an extra-inning home rate fitted on earlier seasons; candidates added in order (team, + park, + starter) by the selection rule.
brain.why: The starter is the largest single pre-game input but is noisy over a few starts, so it is heavily shrunk (tango2007); runs are overdispersed, so a negative binomial beats Poisson; park run environments differ by more than home advantage.

brain.approach: Opponent-adjusted runs for and against, partially pooled team within conference within division (quasi-Poisson MAP with carried priors, realignment-aware), shrunk park effects and connectivity-aware rating uncertainty; a fitted run distribution and an inning-level simulator (seven-inning doubleheaders, measured run rule, walk-offs, extra innings) price every market; starter projections and bullpen availability are tested as a pitcher-aware hybrid.
brain.why: Hundreds of teams with very unequal schedules and few common opponents: shrinkage toward the conference and opponent adjustment matter most, and conference strength is identified only by non-conference games. Rules (seven-inning games, run rule) are measured, not assumed.

sports.label: NBA

brain.approach: Opponent-adjusted offence and defence points ratings (decayed least squares, a ridge pull toward last season carried at a tuned rate) → margin and total; the win curve, margin and total recalibration, their spreads and a back-to-back effect are fitted on earlier seasons' out-of-sample predictions.
brain.why: Points-based ratings are the Massey / adjusted-efficiency family (massey1997, kubatko2007); margins are close to normal (stern1994), so cover and total probabilities follow from the projected mean and an out-of-sample spread.

brain.approach: Designed: opponent-adjusted per-minute rates (significant strikes landed/absorbed, takedowns, control time, submission attempts) driving a Markov chain of fight states → win, method (KO/TKO, submission, decision) and round probabilities, with a Glicko rating as the baseline.
